newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK industry group laments no corporate tax cut.
newsitem.headline: HK industry group laments no corporate tax cut.

text.p: The Federation of Hong Kong Industries said on Thursday that corporate tax cuts should have been given in the territory's 1997/98 budget.
"We regret that there was no reduction in corporate profits tax, particularly in view of the unexpectedly large estimated surplus," chairman Henry Tang said in a statement.

Financial Secretary Donald Tsang on Wednesday unveiled in his budget speech an estimated HK$15.1 billion surplus for the year ending March 31, against an initial forecast of HK$1.6 billion. He predicted a HK$31.7 billion surplus for 1997/98.
But Tsang kept the corporate profit tax rate unchanged at 16.5 percent and the salaries tax rate at 15 percent.
The federation, however, welcomed initiatives to aid the development of the service sector.
"We are glad to hear that money has been earmarked for the first phase of the science park and the building of a second industrial technology centre," Tang said.
"Whilst we agree that those in business are best placed to make decisions on business, the government can help to create an environment which facilitates industry's development," he said.
